question_html: According to Section 4 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, partnership is the relation between persons who have agreed to share the profits of a business carried on by:

options.A: All of them
options.B: Any one of them acting for all
options.C: All or any of them acting for all
options.D: Only the active partners managing the firm

answer_html: Answer: (C) Section 4 defines partnership as the relation between persons who have agreed to share the profits of a business carried on by all or any of them acting for all[cite: 20].

question_html: What is the maximum number of members allowed in a partnership firm under Rule 10 of the Companies (Incorporation) Rules, 2014, pursuant to Section 464 of the Companies Act, 2013?
answer_html: Answer: (C) Rule 10 of Companies (Incorporation) Rules 2014 specifies the maximum limit as 50 members for a partnership firm[cite: 20].

question_html: In the absence of a partnership agreement or deed, what rate of interest is allowed on a partner's loan to the firm?

options.B: 5% per annum
options.C: 6% per annum
options.D: 12% per annum

answer_html: Answer: (C) As per the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, interest at the rate of 6% p.a. is allowed on a partner's loan to the firm in the absence of an agreement[cite: 20].
topic_text: Rules in the Absence of Partnership Deed

question_html: Can a minor be admitted as a partner in a partnership firm?

options.A: Yes, to share both profits and losses equally
options.B: Yes, but only to share the profits of the firm
options.C: No, a minor can never be associated with a partnership firm
options.D: Yes, as a full-fledged partner with unlimited liability

answer_html: Answer: (B) A minor can be added to a partnership firm, but the condition is that he can be admitted to share profits only and cannot share losses[cite: 20].

question_html: Under the Fixed Capital Method, where are adjustments such as interest on capital, partner's salary, and share of profit recorded?

options.A: Partners' Capital Accounts
options.B: Partners' Current Accounts
options.C: Profit and Loss Account directly
options.D: General Reserve Account

answer_html: Answer: (B) Under the fixed capital method, initial capital balances remain unchanged, and all subsequent transactions/adjustments are dealt with through current accounts[cite: 20].

question_html: What is the minimum number of designated partners required in a Limited Liability Partnership (LLP), and how many must be resident in India?

options.A: At least one, and all must be resident in India
options.B: At least two individuals, and at least one must be resident in India
options.C: At least three, and two must be resident in India
options.D: At least two, with no residency requirement

answer_html: Answer: (B) Every LLP should have at least two designated partners who are individuals and at least one of them should be a resident in India[cite: 20].

question_html: How is the term 'resident in India' for a designated partner defined under the LLP Act, 2008 (as amended by the LLP Amendment Act, 2021)?

options.A: Stay in India for not less than 182 days during the immediately preceding one year
options.B: Stay in India for a period of not less than 120 days during the immediately preceding one year
options.C: Stay in India for not less than 90 days during the current financial year
options.D: Stay in India for not less than 180 days during the current financial year

answer_html: Answer: (B) 'Resident in India' means a person who has stayed in India for a period of not less than 120 days during the immediately preceding one year[cite: 20].
topic_text: Definition of Resident in India for LLP

question_html: Which account is debited when interest on capital is allowed to partners?

options.A: Profit and Loss Account
options.B: Profit and Loss Appropriation Account
options.C: Trading Account
options.D: Interest Expense Account

answer_html: Answer: (B) Interest on capital is an appropriation of profit and is debited to the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account[cite: 20].

question_html: What is the legal status of a Limited Liability Partnership (LLP)?

options.A: It has no separate legal entity from its partners.
options.B: It is a body corporate formed and incorporated under the LLP Act, separate from its partners.
options.C: It is governed solely by the Indian Partnership Act, 1932.
options.D: It is treated as a Hindu Undivided Family entity.

answer_html: Answer: (B) A limited liability partnership is a body corporate formed and incorporated under this Act and is a legal entity separate from that of its partners[cite: 20].

question_html: In the absence of any partnership agreement, how are profits and losses to be shared among partners?

options.A: In proportion to their capital contributions
options.B: Equally
options.C: In ratio of time devoted to the business
options.D: As determined by the majority of partners

answer_html: Answer: (B) In the absence of any agreement to the contrary, profits and losses are to be shared equally[cite: 20].
topic_text: Profit Sharing in Absence of Deed

question_html: Are registration requirements mandatory for an ordinary partnership firm and an LLP respectively?

options.A: Voluntary for partnership firm and mandatory for LLP
options.B: Mandatory for both partnership firm and LLP
options.C: Voluntary for both partnership firm and LLP
options.D: Mandatory for partnership firm and voluntary for LLP

answer_html: Answer: (A) Registration of a partnership firm is voluntary, whereas registration of an LLP is mandatory under the LLP Act, 2008[cite: 20].
topic_text: Distinction between Partnership Firm and LLP

question_html: What happens to the existence of an LLP upon the death, insanity, retirement, or insolvency of a partner?

options.A: The LLP is automatically dissolved.
options.B: The existence of the LLP is not affected as it has perpetual succession.
options.C: The LLP must re-register under a new name.
options.D: Its operations are suspended for six months.

answer_html: Answer: (B) An LLP has perpetual succession; the death, insanity, retirement, or insolvency of partner(s) does not affect its existence[cite: 20].

question_html: Which of the following acts as a governing document determining mutual rights and duties of partners in an LLP?

options.A: Articles of Association
options.B: Limited Liability Partnership Agreement
options.C: Partnership Deed under Indian Partnership Act, 1932
options.D: Memorandum of Understanding

answer_html: Answer: (B) 'Limited liability partnership agreement' means any written agreement determining mutual rights and duties of partners and their relation to the LLP[cite: 20].

question_html: Can foreign nationals become partners in a Limited Liability Partnership (LLP)?

options.A: No, foreign nationals are strictly prohibited.
options.B: Yes, foreign nationals can become a partner in an LLP.
options.C: Only if they hold dual citizenship in India.
options.D: Only if they act as designated partners residing in India for 365 days.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Foreign nationals can become a partner in an LLP, unlike traditional partnership firms where foreign nationals face restrictions[cite: 20].
topic_text: Foreign Nationals as Partners in LLP

question_html: What is the limitation of liability of a partner in an ordinary partnership firm compared to an LLP?

options.A: Liability is limited to agreed capital contribution in both cases.
options.B: Liability is unlimited in an ordinary partnership firm, whereas it is limited to agreed contribution in an LLP.
options.C: Liability is limited in ordinary partnership and unlimited in LLP.
options.D: Liability is unlimited in both cases.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Liability of each partner is unlimited in an ordinary partnership firm, whereas in an LLP, partner liability is limited to agreed contribution except in case of willful fraud[cite: 20].

question_html: A, B and C are partners sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 2:3:5. Their fixed capitals were ₹15,00,000, ₹30,00,000 and ₹60,00,000 respectively. For the year 2022, interest on capital was credited to them @ 12% instead of 10%. What will be the net adjustment entry required?

options.A: Debit C's Current Account by ₹15,000; Credit A's Current Account by ₹12,000 and B's Current Account by ₹3,000
options.B: Debit A's Current Account by ₹12,000 and B's by ₹3,000; Credit C's by ₹15,000
options.C: Debit C's Current Account by ₹12,000; Credit A's Current Account by ₹15,000
options.D: Debit A and B equally and credit C

answer_html: Answer: (A) Based on the calculation of excess credit reversal and profit distribution ratio (2:3:5), C's current account is debited by ₹15,000 while A and B are credited by ₹12,000 and ₹3,000 respectively[cite: 20].

question_html: Shilpa and Sanju are partners with capitals of ₹1,00,000 and ₹1,60,000 on January 1, 2022. Shilpa introduced additional capital of ₹30,000 on July 1, 2022 and another ₹20,000 on October 31, 2022. What is the total interest on capital for Shilpa at 9% p.a. for the year ending 2022?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Interest on Shilpa's capital: ₹1,00,000 for 12 months (₹9,000) + ₹30,000 for 6 months (₹1,350) + ₹20,000 for 2 months (₹300) = ₹10,650[cite: 20].
topic_text: Interest on Capital Calculation with Additions

question_html: Partner X drew the following sums: ₹500 on Feb 28, ₹400 on March 31, ₹600 on June 30, and ₹800 on Oct 31, 2022. Accounts close on Dec 31. What is the total interest on drawings at 6% per annum using the product method?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Total product of drawings = 13,800. Interest for 1 month at 6% p.a. on 13,800 is ₹69[cite: 20].

question_html: A and B formed a partnership with capital contributions of ₹50,000 and ₹30,000 on Jan 1, 2022, sharing profits in the capital ratio. Total capital products calculated over 12 months for A and B were found to be ₹6,40,000 and ₹4,00,000 respectively. What is their profit-sharing ratio?
answer_html: Answer: (B) The capital ratio based on products is 64:40, which simplifies to 8:5[cite: 20].

question_html: Weak, Able, and Lazy share profits in the ratio 2:1:1. Draft net profit for 2022 is ₹60,000 before adjustments. Rectifications include: Life insurance of Weak (₹750) charged to Misc Expenditure; Machinery repairs (₹10,000) wrongly capitalized with 20% depreciation charged thereon; Travelling expenses of Able for pleasure trip (₹3,000) charged to travelling expenses. What is the adjusted net profit?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Adjusted Net Profit = ₹60,000 + ₹750 (drawings) + ₹3,000 (drawings) - ₹10,000 (repairs) + ₹2,000 (depreciation reversal) = ₹55,750[cite: 20].

question_html: Ram and Rahim are partners sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3:2. Chief clerk Ratan is admitted as a partner entitled to 1/10th of net profits, with his share of profits in excess of what he would have got as chief clerk taken out of Ram's share. If net profit is ₹1,10,000 and Ratan's prior salary was ₹500 p.m. plus 4% commission on net profits after deducting salary and commission, what is Ram's final share of profit?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Ratan's clerk earnings = ₹6,000 salary + ₹4,000 commission = ₹10,000. Ratan's partner share = 1/10th of ₹1,10,000 = ₹11,000. Excess ₹1,000 is taken from Ram, leaving Ram's share at ₹59,000[cite: 20].

question_html: A, B and C entered into partnership on 01.04.2021 sharing profits in 5:3:2 ratio. A personally guaranteed that C's share of profit after 5% interest on capitals would not be less than ₹30,000. Capitals are ₹3,20,000, ₹2,000,000 (Wait, ₹2,00,000), and ₹1,60,000 respectively. Net profit before interest was ₹1,59,000. What is C's final credited profit amount after guarantee adjustment?
answer_html: Answer: (B) C's initial share of divisible profit (₹1,25,000 * 2/10 = ₹25,000) plus interest on capital (₹8,000) equals ₹33,000, but wait: C's total profit including interest is guaranteed, or share of profit after interest is guaranteed? Per problem text, C's share after interest is guaranteed to be not less than ₹30,000. Divisible profit after interest is ₹1,25,000. C's share is ₹25,000, deficiency of ₹5,000 is met by A, making C's profit share ₹30,000[cite: 20].

question_html: A and B are partners sharing profits in the ratio of effective capital. Opening capitals are ₹1,00,000 and ₹60,000 on Jan 1, 2022. A introduced ₹10,000 on April 1, ₹5,000 on July 1, and withdrew ₹40,000 on Sept 30. B introduced ₹30,000 on July 1. What is the effective capital product total for Partner A?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Total effective capital product for A equals ₹12,00,000, resulting in an effective capital ratio of 12:9 (or 4:3)[cite: 20].

question_html: X and Y are partners where interest on drawings is charged at 10% p.a. X withdrew ₹40,000 per month at the end of each month, and Y withdrew ₹1,20,000 at the end of each quarter. What is the interest on drawings for Partner X for the year ended March 31, 2022?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Interest on X's drawings = ₹4,80,000 * 10/100 * (5.5 / 12) = ₹22,000[cite: 20].

question_html: A, B and C were partners sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3:2. They admitted C for 1/6th share with a guaranteed minimum profit of ₹250,00,000. Total profits were ₹900,00,000. If the guarantee is given by A alone, what is A's final share of profit?
answer_html: Answer: (B) A's normal share (3/6 of 900,00,000 = 4,50,000,000) minus deficiency borne for C (1,00,00,000) = ₹3,50,00,000[cite: 20].

question_html: What is required to create a partnership relation between parties?

options.A: A formal compulsory registration with the Registrar of Firms
options.B: A contract or agreement between parties, which may be written or oral
options.C: Status arising from birth in a Hindu Undivided Family
options.D: A mandatory certificate of incorporation from the Central Government

answer_html: Answer: (B) As per section 5 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, partnership relation arises from contract between parties and not from status; a written agreement is not strictly mandatory[cite: 20].

question_html: Which of the following is considered an implied power of a partner in a trading partnership firm?

options.A: Submitting a dispute relating to the firm to arbitration
options.B: Opening a bank account on behalf of the firm in the name of an individual partner
options.C: Buying and selling of goods
options.D: Acquiring immovable property belonging to the firm without partner consent

answer_html: Answer: (C) Buying and selling of goods is part of the implied powers of partners in a trading firm[cite: 20].

question_html: What is the primary objective of preparing a Profit and Loss Appropriation Account?

options.A: To ascertain the net operating profit or loss of the business from third-party transactions
options.B: To record the distribution of net profit or loss among partners after adjustments like salary and interest
options.C: To calculate gross profit from manufacturing activities
options.D: To list all fixed and current assets of the firm

answer_html: Answer: (B) Profit is divided between partners in a certain ratio after making adjustments like interest, salaries, etc., using the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account[cite: 20].
topic_text: Profit and Loss Appropriation Account Purpose

question_html: Under the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, are partners entitled to a salary or remuneration as a matter of right?

options.A: Yes, standard market salary must be paid to working partners.
options.B: No partner has the right to a salary unless expressly provided in the partnership deed.
options.C: Yes, if they work full-time.
options.D: Only if approved by the Registrar of Firms.

answer_html: Answer: (B) In the absence of an agreement to the contrary, no partner has the right to a salary[cite: 20].

question_html: How does the Fluctuating Capital Method differ from the Fixed Capital Method regarding capital account balances?

options.A: Capital account balances remain completely constant under the fluctuating method.
options.B: Capital account balances fluctuate every time under the fluctuating method as all transactions pass through it, whereas fixed capital keeps initial contributions stable.
options.C: Current accounts are mandatory under fluctuating capital.
options.D: No drawings can be made under fluctuating capital.

answer_html: Answer: (B) In fluctuating capital method, no current account is maintained and all transactions pass through capital accounts, causing balances to fluctuate all the time[cite: 20].

question_html: What is mutual agency in the context of a partnership firm?

options.A: Partners are agents of mutual funds.
options.B: The business is carried on by all or any of them acting for all, making them both principals and agents.
options.C: Partners can act independently without binding the firm.
options.D: Only designated individuals can manage external contracts.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Mutual agency means the business is carried on by all or any of them acting for all, standing in positions of principals and agents[cite: 20].

question_html: What financial disclosures and return filings are required for an LLP under the LLP Act?

options.A: LLPs are completely exempt from filing any annual returns.
options.B: Every LLP must prepare a Statement of Account and Solvency annually and file it with the Registrar.
options.C: Filing is optional depending on partner consensus.
options.D: Only tax returns with the Income Tax department are required, with no Registrar filings.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Every LLP should within six months of financial year end prepare a Statement of Account and Solvency and file it with the Registrar every year[cite: 20].

question_html: Are the provisions of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 automatically applicable to a Limited Liability Partnership?

options.A: Yes, fully applicable.
options.B: No, save as otherwise provided, the provisions of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 shall not apply to an LLP.
options.C: Applicable only during liquidation.
options.D: Applicable only if specified in the LLP agreement.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Save as otherwise provided, the provisions of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932 shall not apply to a limited liability partnership[cite: 20].
topic_text: Non-applicability of Indian Partnership Act to LLP

question_html: What happens if the number of partners in an LLP is reduced below two and it carries on business for more than six months with knowledge of this fact?

options.A: The sole remaining partner becomes personally liable for the obligations of the LLP incurred during that period.
options.B: The LLP is automatically converted into a sole proprietorship by law.
options.C: A fine of 1,000 is levied with no personal liability.
options.D: The partners face imprisonment.

answer_html: Answer: (A) If partners are reduced below two and business continues for more than six months, the sole remaining partner having knowledge shall be personally liable for obligations incurred[cite: 20].
topic_text: Minimum Partners in LLP and Liability

question_html: What is the effect of non-registration of a partnership firm?

options.A: The partnership contract becomes completely void and illegal.
options.B: It restricts the partners or the firm from taking legal action (e.g., suing third parties).
options.C: Partners lose their right to share profits.
options.D: Taxes cannot be filed.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Registration of the firm is not compulsory, but non-registration restricts the partners or the firm from taking any legal action[cite: 20].

question_html: A and B started business on Jan 1, 2022 with capitals of ₹30,000 and ₹20,000. Deed provides B salary of ₹500/month and 6% p.a. interest on opening capitals. Remaining profits shared in 5:3 ratio. Profit before salary and interest was ₹25,000. What is the final profit transferred to A's capital account?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Net profit ₹25,000 - B's salary (₹6,000) - Interest on capitals (A: ₹1,800 + B: ₹1,200 = ₹3,000) = Divisible profit ₹16,000. A's share (5/8 of ₹16,000) = ₹10,000[cite: 20].

question_html: Ram, Rahim and Karim have no partnership agreement. Net profit before claims was ₹45,000. Karim advanced a loan of ₹2,000 to the firm. What amount of net profit remains for appropriation after correctly accounting for Karim's loan interest at default statutory rate?
answer_html: Answer: (B) Interest on Karim's loan at 6% p.a. (since agreement is absent) for 1 year = ₹120. Charged to P&L, leaving ₹45,000 - ₹120 = ₹44,880 for appropriation[cite: 20].
topic_text: Interest on Loan Charge against Profit

question_html: Ram and Rahim start business with capitals of ₹50,000 and ₹30,000 on Jan 1, 2022. Rahim has a salary of ₹400/month. Interest on capitals and drawings is 6% p.a. Profits are distributed equally after adjustments. Capitals are fixed. Ram withdrew ₹8,000 and Rahim ₹10,000. What is Ram's closing Current Account balance?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Ram's Current Account credits: Interest on capital ₹3,000 + Profit share ₹10,470 = ₹13,470. Debits: Drawings ₹8,000 + Interest on drawings ₹240 = ₹8,240. Closing balance = ₹13,470 - ₹8,240 = ₹5,230[cite: 20].

question_html: A and B were partners sharing profits and losses in 3:2 ratio. They admitted C for 1/6th share with guaranteed minimum profit of ₹250,00,000. Total profits were ₹900,00,000. If guarantee is given by A and B equally, what is B's final share of profit?
answer_html: Answer: (B) B's normal share (2/6 of 900,00,000 = 3,00,000,000) minus deficiency borne for C equally (50,00,000) = ₹2,50,00,000[cite: 20].

question_html: In an incomplete question for X and Y, net profit is ₹14,48,000, interest on drawings is ₹40,000 (X: ₹22,000, Y: ₹18,000), salary to X is ₹3,60,000, interest on capital is total ₹2,88,000 (X: ₹1,60,000, Y: ?). What is Y's interest on capital?
answer_html: Answer: (A) Y's Interest on Capital = Total Interest on Capital (₹2,88,000) - X's Interest on Capital (₹1,60,000) = ₹1,28,000[cite: 20].

question_html: What is the primary definition of a 'Small Limited Liability Partnership' under the LLP Act?

options.A: Contribution does not exceed ₹25 lakh and turnover does not exceed ₹40 lakh (within prescribed ceilings up to ₹5 crore and ₹50 crore respectively)
options.B: Contribution does not exceed ₹10 lakh
options.C: Partnership with exactly two partners
options.D: Firm with zero turnover

answer_html: Answer: (A) A small limited liability partnership means an LLP whose contribution and turnover do not exceed prescribed thresholds (contribution up to ₹5 crore and turnover up to ₹50 crore)[cite: 20].

question_html: Are audits mandatory for all Limited Liability Partnerships (LLPs) under the LLP Act?

options.A: Yes, without any exception.
options.B: No, the Central Government may exempt any class or classes of LLPs from audit requirements, and benchmarks apply.
options.C: Audits are never required for LLPs.
options.D: Audits are voluntary for foreign LLPs only.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Accounts of an LLP must be audited, provided the Central Government may exempt any class or classes of LLPs from audit requirements[cite: 20].

question_html: What are the responsibilities of a designated partner in an LLP regarding compliance?

options.A: Responsible for doing all acts, filings, documents, returns, and statements required by the Act, and liable to all penalties.
options.B: Responsible only for raising equity capital.
options.C: Responsible exclusively for internal dispute resolution.
options.D: No statutory responsibility.

answer_html: Answer: (A) A designated partner is responsible for compliance with provisions, including document filing, and is liable to all penalties imposed for contravention[cite: 20].

question_html: Under what circumstances does the liability of an LLP and its partners become unlimited?

options.A: In case of regular business losses
options.B: In case of acts carried out with intent to defraud creditors or for any fraudulent purpose
options.C: Whenever turnover exceeds ₹10 crore
options.D: When a partner retires

answer_html: Answer: (B) The liability of the LLP and partners who are found to have acted with intent to defraud creditors or for any fraudulent purpose shall be unlimited[cite: 20].
topic_text: Fraudulent Activity and Unlimited Liability in LLP

question_html: How is interest on drawings treated in partner capital/current accounts and P&L appropriation?

options.A: Credited to partner accounts and debited to P&L appropriation
options.B: Debited to partner capital/current accounts and credited to Profit and Loss Appropriation Account
options.C: Ignored in appropriation
options.D: Debited to Trading Account

answer_html: Answer: (B) Interest on drawings is debited to the partner's capital/current account and credited to the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account[cite: 20].

question_html: What is the status of a partner's loan to a partnership firm if there is no agreement regarding interest?

options.A: No interest is payable.
options.B: Interest at 6% p.a. must be allowed as a charge against profit.
options.C: Interest at 12% p.a. is allowed as an appropriation.
options.D: Interest is determined by partner vote.

answer_html: Answer: (B) Interest at the rate of 6% p.a. is to be allowed on a partner's loan to the firm as a charge against profit[cite: 20].

question_html: Which individuals are disqualified from becoming a partner in a Limited Liability Partnership?

options.A: Persons of unsound mind, undischarged insolvents, or those who applied to be adjudicated as insolvent with pending applications
options.B: Non-residents only
options.C: Corporate bodies
options.D: Persons below 25 years of age

answer_html: Answer: (A) An individual of unsound mind, an undischarged insolvent, or someone with a pending insolvency adjudication application cannot become an LLP partner[cite: 20].

question_html: What does the suffix of a Limited Liability Partnership name mandatorily contain?

options.A: Limited Company
options.B: LLP or Limited Liability Partnership
options.C: & Co.
options.D: Regulated Partnership

answer_html: Answer: (B) Name of the LLP must contain the words 'limited liability partnership' or its acronym 'LLP' as suffix[cite: 20].

question_html: How are books of accounts maintained by an LLP?

options.A: On cash or accrual basis and according to the double-entry system of accounting, maintained at its registered office
options.B: Only on single entry single-column cash basis
options.C: Maintained exclusively at partner residences
options.D: Maintained only in electronic spreadsheet format without double entry

answer_html: Answer: (A) Every LLP should maintain proper books of accounts on cash or accrual basis and according to double-entry system at its registered office[cite: 20].

question_html: What is the principal difference in the capital account structure between sole proprietorship and partnership firms?

options.A: Partnership firms use capital accounts for each partner, whereas sole proprietorship uses only one capital account.
options.B: Partnership firms cannot have current accounts.
options.C: Sole proprietorship uses multiple capital accounts.
options.D: There is no difference whatsoever.

answer_html: Answer: (A) The only difference is that instead of one capital account in a sole proprietorship, there will be as many capital accounts as there are partners in a partnership firm[cite: 20].
